topic.readerProblem: Online-store owners want to know how ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google AI find and recommend products, and which fixes (feeds, schema, copy, third-party proof, bot access) actually matter first.
topic.connection: AEOeye audits whether AI engines name a brand when buyers ask; for stores that means product-discovery questions, crawler access and the sources engines read, which is what this guide covers.

assessment: The page now explains the documented product-discovery routes for ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews/AI Mode and Perplexity, then gives a template-level checklist for Product markup matched to visible text, buying-question copy, third-party proof, and the technical faults (bot walls, JavaScript-only data, robots rules). It rests on vendor documentation and AEOeye's own crawler access study (e-commerce group, with n and limits). It deliberately does not claim that feeds or schema cause recommendations, does not describe ChatGPT shopping research features (OpenAI's help pages could not be fetched), and cites Perplexity's Merchant Program only through a dated secondary report.

sources.supports: Agentic Commerce Protocol is an open standard letting ChatGPT ingest structured catalog data and surface relevant products.

OAI-SearchBot surfaces sites in ChatGPT search; OpenAI recommends allowing it and its IP ranges; OAI-SearchBot and GPTBot are independent settings; ChatGPT-User may not follow robots.txt; ~24h for robots.txt changes.
No additional requirements or special optimizations or new machine-readable files for AI Overviews/AI Mode; keep Merchant Center info current; structured data must match visible text.
Required (price, currency, Offer) and recommended (GTIN, brand, ratings, reviews, shipping, returns) merchant listing properties; Google may verify merchant listing data.
Structured data must be a true representation of the page content and match visible content.
January 2026 announcement of checkout in AI Mode for eligible U.S. retailers and the Universal Commerce Protocol.
December 2024 analysis: major AI crawlers (OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot) do not render JavaScript.
Server-side or pre-rendering is still a great idea because not all bots can run JavaScript.
Verified bots are validated via Web Bot Auth, published IP lists and reverse DNS; customers can configure AI bot policies.
PerplexityBot surfaces sites in Perplexity search; Perplexity-User generally ignores robots.txt.
Secondary report (WebFX via Stacker, 13 March 2026): Perplexity Merchant Program is free and requires selling and shipping to the U.S. Perplexity's own pages returned 403 to fetchers.
GTIN definition: an identifier for trade items developed by GS1.
